about: A server backup as backup.mjs makes it: the archive, its manifest beside it, the folder they sit in, and the tar command lines (backups go through the system tar, tar.mjs). A 1.x build must restore a 2.0 backup and the reverse. test/contracts-files.test.mjs backs up a stopped server in a scratch data root (standard and full scopes) and compares names, manifest text and archive members; the tar argument lists are held against the source.

layout.archive: <label slug>_<scope>_<stamp>.tar.gz, the label slug being the label with every character outside [A-Za-z0-9_-] turned into -, and absent without a label; a second backup in the same second gets _2, _3 before .tar.gz
layout.stamp: util.mjs stamp: YYYY-MM-DD_HHMMSS in the machine's LOCAL time zone (createdAt in the manifest is UTC)
layout.pending: tar writes <archive>.pending (reserved with an exclusive create, see locks.json), renamed to the archive only after the manifest is written
layout.lock: .snapshot.lock in the folder serialises backups of one server (locks.json)
layout.mirror: with settings.backupsMirrorDir, the archive and manifest are copied to <mirror>/<server>/ and deletions follow

manifest.text: util.mjs writeJson: JSON.stringify(manifest, null, 2) and \n, through manifest.json.tmp
keyOrder: excluded (only when the server leaves paths out)
manifest.lockAndNote: setSnapshotLocked and setSnapshotNote rewrite the manifest as { ...manifest, ...patch }: locked and note are added at the end. A note has tabs and newlines turned into spaces, is trimmed and cut to 80 characters; an empty note is stored as null. A backup with no manifest gets one holding only the patch.

placeholders.<size>: the archive size in bytes, an integer

manifest.afterLockAndNote:
{
  "instance": "survival",
  "scope": "standard",
  "label": null,
  "changeCopy": false,
  "taskId": null,
  "members": [
    "plugins",
    "world",
    "other_world",
    "server.properties",
    "eula.txt"
  ],
  "databases": [],
  "sourceDir": "<data>/instances/survival",
  "createdAt": "<at>",
  "size": "<size>",
  "serverWasRunning": false,
  "flushed": false,
  "skipped": [],
  "warnings": [],
  "locked": true,
  "note": "before the upgrade"
}

members.rule: backup.mjs membersFor. plugins: plugins/ then mods/. worlds: the folders server.properties names (level-name, then its _nether and _the_end) that exist, then every other top folder with a level.dat, in readdir order. config: the root config files that exist, in ROOT_CONFIG_FILES order, then config/. standard is plugins + worlds + config. full is every top-level entry in readdir order except cache, libraries, versions and logs. The server's backupExclude paths are then dropped, and each member goes through tarMember.
members.listingNote: tar -tzf output with / separators, trailing slashes dropped, sorted; archive order is tar's own walk and is not part of the contract. session.lock is never in an archive.

tar.binary: tar.mjs tarBinary: %SystemRoot%\System32\tar.exe on Windows when it exists (bsdtar; never an MSYS GNU tar on PATH), else tar from PATH. runTar treats exit 1 as success (bsdtar warnings on a live server) and anything else as failure.

calls.what: create a backup, cwd the server folder
args: <-C <dump dir> databases, when databases were dumped>

calls.what: unpack a .tar.gz from the file browser
export a world as a zip when the tar can write zip (bsdtar: Windows, macOS); otherwise zip.mjs writes it (zip.json)

databaseDumps.asserted: source (a dump needs a running database)
databaseDumps.about: A database backup (services.mjs backupDatabase): <data>/services/<db>/backups/<tag>_<stamp>.sql, written as .pending and renamed, with <tag>_<stamp>.json beside it. Unlike every other manifest this one is JSON.stringify(value, null, 2) with NO trailing newline, written with fs.promises.writeFile.
